name: Maragua
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; attested only by wordlists (von Martius 1867, Ramirez 2001); no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. & Hélène B. Brijnen. 2015. Johann Natterer and the Amazonian languages. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 6(2): 333-352.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Marawá stress. Only mentions (p. 336) that Natterer's Basel wordlists include 'Marawá (Marauiá)' among two 'apparently extinct (or unidentified) languages.. south of the Amazon river'; no Marawá data reproduced; discussion of Natterer's acute accent (pp. 339-340) concerns Bororo/Baniwa examples and vowel quality, not stress.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: EDUA. xi+796 pp. Ch. 9 'Juruá-Jutaí' (Marawa + Waraiku), pp. 531-553.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number PM5476 .R36 2001
sources.note: Nothing for Marawa. The chapter (pp. 531-535) says only short wordlists exist (Spix in Martius 1863; Tastevin 1920 ms. from Caapiranga), gives a few sound correspondences, pronouns and affixes, then prints the wordlists (pp. 535-553). Tastevin's column carries acute accents on many forms (nalúne 'afraid', akadiutáhõ 'after', nu-bíra 'animal', ukái 'arrow', parúmi 'wind', asíumíhu 'woman'), the Spix column none; no accent rule or remark anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent acento/tônic within it: none). The book's stress sections (2.1.5, 3.1.5, 3.2.5, 4.3.10) concern B…

sources.citation: Tastevin, Constant. 1919. Quelques considérations sur les Indiens du Juruá. BMSAP 6e sér. 10: 144-154 (full PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only the HTML introduction was readable; full text is on Persée behind an altcha challenge. Ethnographic; low chance of a stress remark.

sources.citation: von Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp. 1867 [1863]. Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen (Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II). Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. 'Marauha' wordlist pp. 223-225 (PDF pp. 249-251), footnote '*) Von Spix am Rio Jatahy aufgenommen.'
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. A Latin-glossed wordlist of c. 200 items recorded by Spix on the Rio Jutaí, with no accent marks and no phonological note; Martius's general remark that the acute accent 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' (p. 29) belongs to the Tupi dictionary section and is not applied to the Marauha list.
